newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-IAAF DELAYS CAPOBIANCO DRUGS HEARING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF DELAYS CAPOBIANCO DRUGS HEARING.

text.p: The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) acceded to legal pressure on Thursday and delayed the arbitration hearing for the drugs case of Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco.
The arbitration panel of the IAAF was due to discuss the case on November 24 but bowed to the requests from the lawyers of both parties to postpone the hearing to a date which has yet to be set.
Capobianco tested positive for the steroid stanozolol, the drug used by Ben Johnson at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, at a meeting in the Dutch town of Hengelo last May.
He escaped a four-year ban when his national governing body Athletics Australia cleared him on the grounds that the testing procedures had been seriously flawed.
The IAAF opposed that decision but Capobianco was allowed to compete at the Atlanta Olympics after their legal advisors said the federation could be sued successfully in a civil court.

The hearing of Italian high jumper Antonella Bevilacqua, who was also permitted to take part in the Olympics after the Italian panel judged that her two positive tests for the stimulant ephedrine in May were an accident, will go ahead as planned on November 25.
